tests/fixtures/stripboard/ - HC8's benchmark fixtures
=====================================================

Six files, in two groups.

B2's FROZEN LOW-BOOST BENCHMARK - the board B1-frozen is stated against:

  pultec-low-boost-frozen.vrt      the owner's hand layout, byte for byte as it
                                   stood at commit 2f62ee1
  pultec-low-boost-frozen.netlist  the EESchema v1.1 netlist export of the
                                   electrical model as it stood at that same
                                   commit - the model the hand layout was built
                                   against. 9 nets, 27 pins.
  pultec-low-boost-frozen.dump     the pinned binary's --dump-board on that .vrt

THE THREE FURTHER BENCHMARK BOARDS of PIPELINE 3.5, as --dump-board captures
of the .vrt committed under boards/. Their reference netlists are NOT copied
here: each already has a committed export in tests/fixtures/, and a second copy
is a second thing to keep in step.

  pt2399-core.dump                 reference: tests/fixtures/pt2399-core-veroroute.net
  transistor-preamp-feedback.dump  reference: tests/fixtures/transistor-preamp-feedback.net
  transistor-preamp-staged.dump    reference: tests/fixtures/transistor-preamp-staged.net

WHY THESE FILES EXIST, AND WHY THEY ARE COMMITTED RATHER THAN REGENERATED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
They are what tests/stripboard/agreement.test.ts grades HC8 against: the
reconstruction must partition each board's pins exactly as that board's
reference netlist does, on four boards nobody here laid out.

The low-boost three are FROZEN, and that is the whole point of them. B1-frozen
is stated against "the exact electrical model, footprints and board dimensions
the hand layout was built for - 9 nets, 27 pins", and today's scaffolded
low-boost model is a different circuit: 14 nets and 40 pins. Regenerating the
export would quietly restate the benchmark against the newer circuit and report
the result as a comparison with a 9-net hand layout.

THEY LIVE UNDER tests/fixtures/ AND NEVER UNDER boards/, which is B2's own
rule: `make -C boards/<board> check` regenerates the export every run and
decides freshness by content, so a deliberately frozen model under boards/ is a
deliberately stale one the freshness guard would be right to fail. The fixture
goes where the guard does not run, rather than the guard being weakened.

The three further dumps are committed for the reason
tests/fixtures/pt2399-core-board.dump was: a dump is the readable form of a
board, and a test can assert over it without spawning the binary. They are
reproducible from the .vrt files beside them and their hashes are below, so a
silently edited one surfaces as a changed hash rather than as a quietly easier
test.

HOW THEY WERE MADE - the exact commands, into a scratch directory first, never
over a path under boards/
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  VR=.tools/veroroute-perfboard/veroroute.app/Contents/MacOS/veroroute

  git show 2f62ee1:boards/pultec-low-boost/pultec-low-boost.perfboard.vrt \
      > $SCRATCH/frozen.vrt
  "$VR" --dump-board $SCRATCH/frozen.vrt > $SCRATCH/frozen.dump

  git worktree add --detach $SCRATCH/wt-2f62ee1 2f62ee1
  (in that worktree, a four-line script calling the repository's own export
   path - loadDeclaration() from tools/perfboard/declaration.ts into
   exportNetlistFor() from tools/perfboard/check.ts, which is the same lowering
   `make check` and the write verbs use, so there is no second export path here)
      bun run export-net.ts boards/pultec-low-boost/perfboard.json \
          > $SCRATCH/frozen.netlist
  git worktree remove $SCRATCH/wt-2f62ee1

  "$VR" --dump-board boards/pt2399-core/pt2399-core.perfboard.vrt \
      > tests/fixtures/stripboard/pt2399-core.dump
  "$VR" --dump-board \
      boards/transistor-preamp-feedback/transistor-preamp-feedback.perfboard.vrt \
      > tests/fixtures/stripboard/transistor-preamp-feedback.dump
  "$VR" --dump-board \
      boards/transistor-preamp-staged/transistor-preamp-staged.perfboard.vrt \
      > tests/fixtures/stripboard/transistor-preamp-staged.dump

B2's BENCHMARK, RUN BEFORE ANY TEST WAS WRITTEN. B2: "if the extraction cannot
produce an export agreeing with the fixture board's own 9 NODE and 27 PIN
lines, the fixture is wrong and says which number disagreed". Measured on the
files above: the export has 9 nets and 27 pins; the dump has 9 NODE lines and
27 PIN lines; and the two sides' pin identities agree exactly - no pin in one
and not the other - once the dump's PAD provenance is read (see below). The
same comparison on the other three: 21/65, 11/37 and 22/78, agreeing on both
counts and on every pin identity. Nothing was adjusted to make it agree.

THE ONE FIELD THAT IS NOT BYTE-REPRODUCIBLE: the .netlist's header comment
carries the timestamp the export ran at, `{ EESchema Netlist Version 1.1
created 2026-10-11T08:00:38 }`. A re-run at 2f62ee1 reproduces every other byte
and a different timestamp. The readers strip brace comments before tokenising
(lib/kicad/legacy-netlist.ts), so nothing downstream reads it.

THE PAD LINES, AND WHY HC8 READS THEM. The low-boost export names the off-board
selector and pot terminals RV_LO_BOOST.1..3 and SW_LO_BOOST.1..7, while the
dump's PIN lines name them RV_LO_BOOST_1.1 .. SW_LO_BOOST_7.1: VeroRoute
expands a PADS<n> component into n one-hole pads with board names of their own,
and the dump's `PAD <name> <value> AT <row>,<col> FROM <ref>.<pin>` line is the
only place it records which reference pin each pad is. Ten of this board's
twenty-seven pins are pads. HC8 reads that line for pin identity only, never as
a copper join; see tools/stripboard/pad-provenance.ts.

WHAT MAY NOT BE CONCLUDED FROM IT
---------------------------------
The frozen low-boost fixture is NOT today's low-boost board. It is 9 nets and
27 pins; the scaffolded model is 14 nets and 50 pins, and a figure measured
here says nothing about that board.

  ON THAT 50. PIPELINE 3.4 and D15 both say "14 nets and 40 pins against
  today's model". Measured here by running the same export path against the
  board's declaration at this commit: 14 nets and 50 pin entries, of which 10
  are the off-board pad terminals (PADS3 + PADS7) and 40 are everything else.
  So 40 is the non-pad count and the two figures are the same measurement
  counted two ways, not a disagreement about the circuit - but 40 is not the
  number the export's own pin entries total, and the figure is recorded both
  ways here rather than one of them being restated without its basis.

B1-frozen's C <= 5 and W = 0 are stated
against THIS model and apply here and nowhere else: C <= 5 at N = 14 would
require nine occupied strips before a single net may split, and W = 0 is a
property of the artifact being reproduced - the owner's layout carries zero
WIRE lines - not a general preference. B1-current is the scaffolded board's own
criterion and carries neither clause.

A PASS HERE IS AGREEMENT WITH A NETLIST, NOT A BUILDABLE BOARD. These files
grade HC8 only. The frozen low-boost board FAILS `make check` today, for the
staleness above, and nothing in this directory is evidence that it does not.

AND IT IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THE BOARDS THAT ARE NOT HERE.
transistor-preamp-lab's dump reports CUT_STATE UNRESOLVED with 19
CUT_CONFLICT lines, so its cut list is absent rather than empty and HC2
excludes it; its export also names J2.1 and J2.2, for which the dump prints no
PIN line. transistor-preamp-loop is COMPUTED but HC8 reports 15 opens on it,
agreeing net for net with the 15 incomplete nets `make check` reports there.
transistor-preamp-buffered agrees and passes `make check`, and is still left
out, because PIPELINE 3.5's set is a specified four rather than every board
that happens to pass. All three are deliberately absent from this directory,
and tests/stripboard/agreement.test.ts names each one and why.
